10617748.reason: Unconditionally subtracts one from the employee component count, omitting the case with no initial language knowledge. The valid two-employee all-zero input requires 2 lessons, but it returns 1.

11352639.reason: On a new employee it unions the language set with only the first intersecting component and breaks, rather than merging every bridged component. Employee 7's languages {7,4} connect the existing {6,7} and {4,5} islands; the stale second island leaves four components instead of three and produces 3 rather than 2 lessons.

11352706.reason: Always returns component_count-1 and misses the no-language-known special case. For two employees with zero languages the necessary teaching cost is 2, whereas this program emits 1.

9220573.reason: Uses the usual component-connection cost components-1 when nobody initially knows any language. For two employees each knowing zero languages, both must learn a language, so the answer is 2, not its 1.

9357260.reason: The any(lang) test checks whether employee Boolean-list objects are nonempty, not whether any language bit is true; each list has m entries even when all are false. It therefore subtracts one even when nobody knows any language, returning 1 instead of the required 2 on the recorded two-employee all-zero input.
